subject: Activation readiness: stakeholder mapping & onboarding path
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Activation readiness: stakeholder mapping & onboarding path

Hi Jordan — thanks again for today's demo and the productive discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep the evaluation moving toward a 4-week hands-on trial: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: validate 95th-percentile generation latency < 300ms for customer-facing routing and show 2x cost improvement vs their current baseline.
- Success criteria: accuracy on the sample prompt set (F1 >= 0.78), latency SLOs met under 200 concurrent sessions, and stable KV cache behavior over a day-long simulation.

Proposed activation path (high level):
1) Week 0: procurement & security intake (collect SOC2 evidence, enable a short IP allowlist).
2) Week 1: infra handoff and staging deployment; integrate with Acme app's API key exchange.
3) Week 2: run the sample prompt suite and synthetic load.
4) Week 3: iterate on prompt templates and quantization settings.
5) Week 4: review results and decide next steps (scale or pilot purchase).

As discussed, we need to lock two internal owners on your side to be effective: an infra/ops point and a procurement contact for the purchase order. Can you confirm who owns infra and who will be the procurement approver? If you prefer, put us in touch with the right people and we will kick off the security questionnaire and a short procurement template.

Action items for Acme (please):
- Confirm infra owner and procurement contact (name + email).
- Share any initial security questionnaire items beyond SOC2 (data residency, logs retention).
- Target start date for trial (you mentioned early May).

Cc'd Laura and Vivek from our side to map internal owners and provide a lightweight deployment plan. I attached a one-page activation checklist in the drive link (see HubSpot).

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.com]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation readiness: stakeholder mapping & onboarding path

Thanks Jasmine — great recap. Quick answers: 

Infra/ops owner: Maya Singh <maya.singh@acme.com> (she owns platform infra and will coordinate network/IPs).
Procurement approver: Tina Alvarez <tina.alvarez@acme.com> (PO and contract routing).
Security contact: security-questions@acme.com (they will triage the SOC2 and any custom intake).

We are comfortable targeting a May 4 start for the 4-week trial. Security will need the questionnaire and a short architectural diagram; I can loop Maya and Tina into the thread if you want.

Two clarifications from our side:
- We will run a representative traffic shape that peaks at ~200 concurrent sessions; can you confirm you can reproduce that shape in staging?
- We prefer the trial to run against our staging cluster with an allowlist for Redwood IPs.

I will also upload our internal compliance checklist. For procurement, Tina typically needs a rough quote and statement of work; Laura, can you provide a one-page SOW/quote?

— Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Logistics
[jordan.lee@acme.com]

Date: Thu, 23 Apr 2026 11:24:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Activation readiness: stakeholder mapping & onboarding path

Forwarding Jordan's reply — they confirmed Maya (infra) and Tina (procurement); security will triage via security-questions@acme.com.

Vivek / Marcus / Laura — can each of you reply with:
- Your proposed owner on Redwood's side to be the direct counterpart (infra, app integration, security, procurement support).
- A short list (3 bullets) of what you need from Acme to start (credentials, diagrams, access windows).
- Any blocking constraints that would prevent a May 4 start.

I captured what we need to own on our side but want clear single-point owners so Jordan's team knows who to contact. Please reply by EOD so I can loop in Acme and Maya/Tina.

Thanks — Jasmine

Subject: Re: Activation readiness: stakeholder mapping & onboarding path

Thanks — quick tech owner notes from my side.

Redwood tech counterpart: Vivek Kulkarni (me) — infra deployment / staging lead.
Responsibilities I will cover:
- Provision dedicated staging capacity and set up prefix/KV caching config for the sample workload.
- Run synthetic load that mirrors their 200 concurrent sessions traffic shape and report latency percentiles.
- Provide a short slide with the endpoint configuration and IPs for allowlisting.

What I need from Acme:
- Staging API endpoint and a test account with basic sample payloads (prefer JSON schema).
- Network window for us to coordinate allowlist changes (ideally a 2-hour window between 09:00–17:00 PT).
- The architectural diagram Jordan mentioned (service-to-service auth, where secrets live).

Blocking constraints for May 4 start:
- I need the allowlist IPs and staging endpoint by EOD Monday (Apr 27) to stand up infra and run initial smoke tests.

Attachment: deployment-plan.pdf (one-page deployment checklist).

I'll hand off SRE runbooks to Laura for integration notes after the first smoke test.

— Vivek
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 25 Apr 2026 11:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Activation readiness: stakeholder mapping & onboarding path

Looping in security perspective and next steps.

Security single point: Marcus Lin (redwood security).
Immediate asks from Acme security team:
- Completed acme-security-questionnaire.xlsx (I attached a blank version).
- Short architecture diagram focused on data flow and retention points.
- Clarify whether logs containing PII will be sent to Redwood. If yes, we need a focused data handling addendum.

Minimum security gating items for trial start:
1) SOC2 in-scope evidence (they can share their last SOC2 summary report).
2) IP allowlist established and verified (Vivek will provide our egress IPs).
3) Confirmed log retention policy (we recommend 30 days for the trial).

I created a Jira ticket to track security intake: https://jira.redwood.com/browse/SEC-912 — please reference it in replies. Once Acme returns the questionnaire and the architecture diagram we can clear security gating in 48–72 hours.

Next steps / timeline (proposed):
- Apr 27: receive allowlist and staging endpoint (Vivek).
- Apr 28–29: security completes triage (Marcus).
- May 4: stand up trial in Acme staging (target).

If anyone wants to pivot timelines, flag it now. I will draft a short security acceptance checklist and post it to the Jira ticket.

— Marcus
Redwood Security
